strongest_objection: The declared type says the tell is read off what the investor spends, forgoes, sequences, or signs 'rather than says', yet five of the eighteen members (Tense switch, Borrowed eyes, Holdable sentence, Named objection, and the unprompted naming in Neighbor in the portfolio) are read off speech. The author rescues each one by naming a cost inside the speech: quotability, the position of a question in the sequence, the specificity of a no. That rescue is the map's real item type, sharper than the one declared: a tell is a cost the investor pays or forgoes without pricing the reading into it, whether the cost sits in a calendar, a signature, or a sentence. The under-stated type has consequences the map pays for. It lets Borrowed eyes collapse into Tense switch on the ordinary case of a lead who asks who else is in first as a competitive check and then inspects, because 'first question' is a sequence fact and not a cost fact; the repair below moves the tell to whether inspection follows the answer. It rules the residue item Wire before paper out on the denominator caveat every admitted item carries, when a partner wiring the fund's own money before paper is the largest unpriced cost on the route. And it leaves the map reading every cost spent inside the fund and on the market while reading none spent toward the founder. The structure otherwise survived: I could not separate the author's Fuse/Exclusivity pair any better than they did, the loop and the fork are real and a sequence would hide both, and no item is a theme or a restatement except one clause of Let it lapse.

items.item: Partner's name on the door: whether the person across the table can carry a deal is read from whose name sits on the fund's last deals, its board seats and its announcements, not from the title on the website, since a venture partner, a principal, or an operating partner can refer but cannot spend; it lies in exactly one case, the newly made partner whose name is on nothing because their first deal is still to come, and who therefore has the strongest motive in the building to close one.
items.why: 'It lies in exactly one case' is false precision promoted to fact. It also lies at the laterally hired partner whose deals sit on another fund's ledger, and at funds that seat a different partner on the board than the one who sponsored the deal, where the seat list reads bandwidth rather than standing.
items.repair: Partner's name on the door: whether the person across the table can carry a deal is read from whose name sits on the fund's last deals, its board seats and its announcements, not from the title on the website, since a venture partner, a principal, or an operating partner can refer but cannot spend; it lies most instructively at the newly made partner whose name is on nothing because their first deal is still to come, and who therefore has the strongest motive in the building to close one, and it also lies at the partner hired laterally, whose deals sit on another fund's ledger, and at funds that seat a different partner on the board than the one who sponsored the deal, where the seat list reads bandwidth and not standing.

items.item: Borrowed eyes: an investor whose first question is who else is in holds a position that is a function of another investor's, so the founder is reading the wrong node and every later tell from this investor should be re-read as a tell about the lead it follows, a day late; it lies when the question is about round mechanics from a fund that never leads and honestly needs a lead to set terms, which its ledger shows as a record of follows.
items.why: Closest-neighbor test against Tense switch: a lead-capable fund that opens with who else is in, hears nobody yet, and then spends the meeting on the past tense is running a competitive check, not borrowing eyes, and as written the item reads it as a follower. The carrier is not the first question but whether inspection follows the answer.
items.repair: Borrowed eyes: an investor who asks who else is in before any question about the company, and whose questions about the company arrive only after the answer names a lead, or never, holds a position that is a function of another investor's, so the founder is reading the wrong node and every later tell from this investor should be re-read as a tell about the lead it follows, a day late; not the same question asked first by an investor who then inspects, which checks whether the round is already spoken for, and it lies when the question is about round mechanics from a fund that never leads and honestly needs a lead to set terms, which its ledger shows as a record of follows.

items.item: Named objection: a no that states the specific objection that won reveals that a vote happened and the sponsor argued and lost, since only someone who fought the objection can name it exactly, while a no attributed to the partnership in generic terms reveals that the deal never reached the room; it adds to deal-deaths' Champion's single-tender want, which reads how a sponsor's leaving kills a deal, by reading from the wording of the no whether a sponsor existed at all, and it lies when a partner who killed the deal alone reads back the founder's own weakest slide as the objection.
items.why: 'Reveals that a vote happened' is asserted as fact, and a specific no that is a fund rule (a stage floor, a sector the fund does not do) is exact without any vote, which the item's only lie case (the solo killer reading back the weakest slide) does not cover. The specificity that carries the tell is particularity to this company, not specificity as such.
items.repair: Named objection: a no that states the objection that won, in terms particular to this company, reads as a vote that happened and a sponsor who argued and lost, since only someone who fought the objection can name it exactly, while a no attributed to the partnership in generic terms reads as a deal that never reached the room; not a specific no that is a fund rule, a stage floor or a sector the fund does not do, which is exact without any vote, and it adds to deal-deaths' Champion's single-tender want, which reads how a sponsor's leaving kills a deal, by reading from the wording of the no whether a sponsor existed at all; it lies when a partner who killed the deal alone reads back the founder's own weakest slide as the objection.

items.item: Back-channel spent: a call to a reference the founder offered is process, but a call to someone the founder did not offer, a former employee, a former investor, a rival's founder, costs the caller a favor and is spent only near the decision, so learning of it, usually from the person called, reads that the partner meeting is close and names the objection being tested; the reverse of lead-time-floors' Seeking is telling, since here the investor's search is visible to the founder, and the sharper reading is the call not made, because a term sheet issued with no back-channel is a reservation and not a decision; it lies at large multi-stage funds whose research staff call everyone at screen, where the favor costs the partner nothing.
items.why: 'A term sheet issued with no back-channel is a reservation and not a decision' is unconditional, and it is wrong at pre-seed, where there is no former employer, former investor, or rival for anyone to call: the absent call reads nothing there, and a sheet without one is a decision made on the founder. The item's lie case covers only the opposite end, the multi-stage fund whose staff call everyone.
items.repair: Back-channel spent: a call to a reference the founder offered is process, but a call to someone the founder did not offer, a former employee, a former investor, a rival's founder, costs the caller a favor and is spent only near the decision, so learning of it, usually from the person called, reads that the partner meeting is close and names the objection being tested; the reverse of lead-time-floors' Seeking is telling, since here the investor's search is visible to the founder, and the sharper reading is the call not made, because a term sheet issued with no back-channel is a reservation and not a decision wherever there was someone to call; it lies at large multi-stage funds whose research staff call everyone at screen, where the favor costs the partner nothing, and it is undefined at pre-seed, where no former employee, investor, or rival exists to be called and the absent call reads nothing.

items.item: Term as forecast: each protective term is a bet on a future state, so the redline shows the investor's private forecast, a participating preference pricing a middling exit as likely, a full ratchet pricing a down round, super pro-rata pricing a wish for more, information rights without a seat pricing a passive hold, as an arms treaty's inspection clauses name the breach each side expects; only deviations from the fund's standard paper read, since house paper forecasts nothing, and the founder learns the standard from other founders who took it; it lies where the partner has not read what counsel sent.
items.why: The item correctly excludes the fund's house paper as forecasting nothing, but a term carried forward from the company's own prior round is neither house paper nor this investor's forecast, and it is the commonest source of a scary term on a later sheet. One lie case is missing.
items.repair: Term as forecast: each protective term is a bet on a future state, so the redline shows the investor's private forecast, a participating preference pricing a middling exit as likely, a full ratchet pricing a down round, super pro-rata pricing a wish for more, information rights without a seat pricing a passive hold, as an arms treaty's inspection clauses name the breach each side expects; only deviations from the fund's standard paper read, since house paper forecasts nothing, and the founder learns the standard from other founders who took it; it lies where the partner has not read what counsel sent, and where a term was carried forward from the company's own prior paper, which forecasts the last investor's fear and not this one's.

items.item: Let it lapse: some tells exist only if the founder moves, so an expiry allowed to pass by a day reads whether the fuse was real, since a re-issued sheet shows the investor feared losing the deal more than being seen to bluff and a withdrawn one shows the clock was the fund's, as a deadline a kidnapper lets pass unacted reveals the deadline was a bluff; likewise offering anonymized accounts reads the shopper and declining the early data room reads whether a partner date appears; not a tell observed but a probe run, at the price of being wrong once, and it lies when the counterparty is not a partner but a committee that records the lapse as a fact.
items.why: The core is one mechanism, but the 'likewise' clause restates Shopping list's anonymization test and Order of asks' date test in probe form; Shopping list already contains its test verbatim. The station is real; the item should point at the sibling probes rather than restate them.
items.repair: Let it lapse: some tells exist only if the founder moves, so an expiry allowed to pass by a day reads whether the fuse was real, since a re-issued sheet shows the investor feared losing the deal more than being seen to bluff and a withdrawn one shows the clock was the fund's, as a deadline a kidnapper lets pass unacted reveals the deadline was a bluff; the same move exists at Shopping list and Order of asks, whose tests become probes when the founder makes the offer or the refusal first; not a tell observed but a probe run, at the price of being wrong once, and it lies when the counterparty is not a partner but a committee that records the lapse as a fact.

items.item: Tense switch: an investor still deciding asks about the past, why the cohort churned, why this architecture, while an investor who has decided asks about the deal, round size, who else is in, whether there is room to lead, and the switch usually precedes any spoken yes by days; the sharpest form is the allocation question, how much can we take, which is addressed to the other investors through the founder, as an auction bidder who asks about the reserve has stopped inspecting the lot; it lies when a partner asks round size first to check the fund's check-size fit, which is a size question and not an allocation question.
items.why: Survives the neighbor test against Borrowed eyes once Borrowed eyes is moved to whether inspection follows; the allocation question addressed to other investors through the founder is a real cost inside speech. 'Usually precedes any spoken yes by days' is a frequency estimate from composite cases and should stay read as such.

items.item: Ledger's clock: whether a yes is even available is read from the fund's own deployment record before the partner's appetite matters, since a fund in year four of a five-year investment period with half its capital uncalled must deploy and a fund that made nine investments in its first year and one in its third is holding reserves for its own portfolio, and both are visible in announced checks and filing dates before the first email; the carrier is the fund's ledger and not the partner, and it lies when the visible fund is not the vehicle that would write this check, an unannounced successor fund or an opportunity vehicle running on a different clock.
items.why: Kept, but the ledger it reads is partial: uncalled capital is not public for most funds and announced checks undercount deployment, so the reading is an estimate from a sample rather than something 'visible'. The boundary claim concedes private ledgers and should concede partial public ones.

neighbor_test.separating_case: Both items read the question who else is in. Case: a fund whose ledger shows it leads half its deals opens the first meeting with who else is in, is told nobody yet, and spends the next hour on why the cohort churned; a week later it asks how much can we take. That is Tense switch (competitive check, inspection, then the allocation question), and the item as written files it under Borrowed eyes because the first question was who else is in. Contrast: the same fund, told Fund X is leading, asks nothing about the company and goes straight to allocation; that is Borrowed eyes. The separating variable is whether inspection follows the answer, not the position of the question, so the pair does not collapse but Borrowed eyes needed its carrier moved (repair above).

boundary_case: The price on the term sheet: it is signed rather than said, it is what the investor spends, and it is the first thing a founder reads. Ruling: out of type. Price is the contested object of the negotiation, the one carrier every party knows is read and prices the reading into, so it reveals only what the investor is willing to say with money and nothing the investor did not mean to show. Term as forecast stays in on exactly that contrast: a protective term is a bet on a state the investor does not control and would rather not state, and the deviation from house paper leaks a forecast the investor did not price into it. The ruling also names the sharper item type the map runs on: a tell is a cost whose reading the investor did not price in.

seriation.note: Endpoints are real (the public record before the first email; the next round after the wire) and the axis is a residence itinerary, declared as such. The hinge adjacency Back-channel spent → Fuse length teaches: the same expiry clause is a reservation or a decision depending on what preceded it, and a founder who reads the fuse without the back-channel reads the wrong object. One soft spot: Tense switch and Borrowed eyes are in-room tells filed after Queue interval (the following week); this is defensible only if they are read as second-meeting tells, which the note should say. Queue interval straddles two stations by design and says so. The prison-yard and auction-reserve cases are used as remote illustrations but are not in the boundary claim's list of simplified remote cases; add them.

edges.why: The loop is real but the label conflates two channels. Ledger's clock reads deployment pace off new announced checks and filings; the post-wire hands (bridges, marks accepted, pro-rata taken) reach the outside as announced participation at best and otherwise only founder to founder, which the item itself says ('the first tell for the next founder'). As written the antecedent is near-definitional and cannot fail; naming the channel makes it a claim.
edges.repair_label: If a fund's post-wire hands (pro-rata taken, gaps bridged, marks accepted) are what its founders could only read too late, and those hands reach the outside as announced participation or founder to founder, then the fund's outside-readable ledger is made of them, so the last tell of one raise is the first tell of the next; where a bridge or a mark stays private the loop closes only through founders who talk, never through the filings, and the loop closes through other founders and never through the same one.

edges.why: 'The tense switch never comes from this investor' overclaims: a follower's own switch does arrive, as an echo, and the echo carries one bit (that the lead has switched). The label should say what the echo reads rather than that it never comes, and should carry the repaired antecedent (inspection never followed).
edges.repair_label: If the first question was who else is in and inspection never followed the answer, then this investor's tense switch is an echo of the lead's, a day later, and reads only that the lead has switched; the founder reads the lead's questions and discards this investor's.

edges.why: Real dependency with a failable antecedent (the ledger may show no must-deploy); a sequence would not show that the interval has no reading until the denominator is read.
The map's best edge: one clause, two objects, the fork keyed on what preceded the sheet. A sequence conceals it.
Passage from observation to experiment; the 'Can test' form is right and the antecedent (the founder chooses to let it pass) can fail.

modality_problems: Partner's name on the door: 'it lies in exactly one case' asserts a count the composite cases cannot support (repaired).
Named objection: 'reveals that a vote happened' promotes an analytical reading to fact, and a rule-based specific no defeats it (repaired).
Back-channel spent: 'a term sheet issued with no back-channel is a reservation and not a decision' is stated unconditionally and fails at pre-seed (repaired).

Ledger's clock: 'visible in announced checks and filing dates' treats a partial public sample (Form D amounts sold, announced rounds) as the fund's deployment record; uncalled capital is not public for most funds and the reading is an estimate.

Tense switch: 'the switch usually precedes any spoken yes by days' is a frequency claim from composite cases with no denominator; acceptable under the declared analytical mode, but it should not be quoted as observed.
Edge Borrowed eyes → Tense switch: 'never comes from this investor' overclaims (repaired).
The prison-yard rank case and the auction-reserve case are folk illustrations not listed in the boundary claim's inventory of simplified remote cases; the inventory should include them.
duplication: none at item level. The of-sentence is importance-detectors' form (carrier read, state revealed, the lie, the residence needed) instantiated for one counterparty, which makes the map a sibling of that list rather than a restatement of it; the shared skeleton is worth naming in the record. Adjacent items say what they add: Queue interval and Exclusivity as confession and Back-channel spent to lead-time-floors (Partner meeting, No-shop, Seeking is telling); Named objection to deal-deaths (Champion's single-tender want); Neighbor in the portfolio to cooperative-masks (the alliance proposed to inventory your capabilities).
best_unresolved_seed: Costs the investor spends toward the founder before the wire: a portfolio founder who calls unprompted to vouch for the partner, a customer introduction made before any sheet, a bridge wired before paper. These are the pre-wire mirror of Next-round hand, the fund spending its own favors or capital to hold a deal it has not yet won, and the map currently reads every cost spent inside the fund and on the market and none spent toward the founder. The residue item Wire before paper belongs here and was rejected on the denominator caveat every admitted item carries, which is not a reason. A cheaper instrument for the same class: deck telemetry, where a second partner's open on the data room is Second body before the meeting happens.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after repairing six items (a false 'exactly one case', a neighbor collapse between Borrowed eyes and Tense switch on the competitive-check case, three missing lie cases at pre-seed, rule-based passes, and carried-forward terms, and one clause of Let it lapse that restated its neighbors) and two edge labels, and after noting that the declared type's 'rather than says' undersells its own members, which are read off the unpriced cost inside a calendar, a signature, or a sentence.
